title: Harmonize scheduler admission windowing to reduce long-context tail and tenant starvation
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Multiple customers (hosted + dedicated) reported sudden SLO regressions: small, latency-sensitive requests experienced 5x tail latency increases during mixed-length traffic spikes. Incidents traced to admission windowing edge cases in the continuous batching scheduler interacting with KV cache warming and eviction, causing short requests to be repeatedly delayed or preempted until long-context batches complete.
steps_to_repro: 1) Start a mixed workload: 60% short requests (<=64 tokens), 40% long-context requests (>=4096 tokens) targeted at the same model endpoint.
2) Configure scheduler with default adaptive admission windowing and no per-tenant short-request reserve.
3) Observe increased queueing for short requests after sustained long-context arrivals and KV cache churn.
4) Reproduce locally using load-generator script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/loadgen/mixed-length (use scenario 'mixed_spike_long_first')
telemetry_summary: Grafana traces showed that during spikes: admission window opened wide to accommodate long-context batches; batch formation delays for short requests increased from 5ms median to 120ms p99; tenant-level in-flight token count exceeded expected weight-based caps; KV-cache eviction rate spiked, causing cache-miss amplification and additional token compute that extended long-batch runtimes.
root_cause: The admission-window heuristics weight batches by request count and estimated token runtime but did not account for multi-tenant fairness when long-context requests continuously re-enter the admission flow. Combined with aggressive KV cache eviction when memory pressure rose, long batches prolonged the processing window and effectively starved short requests. Additionally, the preemption path favored throughput (batch completeness) over latency-sensitive fast-paths, leading to repeated postponement of small requests.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a lightweight per-tenant short-request reserve: keep a small, always-available admission slot pool for latency-sensitive requests (configurable percent of capacity).
2) Adjust admission-window scoring to include a decaying age penalty and estimated finish-time delta so older waiting small requests gain priority over brand-new long requests of similar score.
3) Add an early-exit fast-path that allows microbatches of <64 token requests to bypass full batch formation when waiting time exceeds threshold (feature-flagged).
4) Reduce KV eviction aggressiveness during mixed workloads by tuning soft limits and pre-warming strategies for tenant KV caches under known long-context patterns.
5) Add deterministic unit tests and a chaos test in the loadgen harness that simulates cache churn + long-tail arrivals to prevent regressions.
6) Roll out behind runtime feature flag and canary gates with detailed canary metrics for short-request p50/p95/p99 and tenant fairness index.
acceptance_criteria: - Short-request p99 latency under mixed-length synthetic attack returns to <150ms in canary region (baseline ~40ms).
- No throughput regression >3% for long-context workloads at 90th percentile capacity.
- New telemetry exposes per-tenant fairness index and short-request reserve utilization; alerts fire when reserve exhausted for >60s.
- Unit and integration tests added to CI that reproduce the starvation pattern with deterministic outcomes.
- Rollout plan documented and signed off by SRE and Product (see attachments).
rollout_plan: 1) Implement behind feature flag; run unit tests + integration harness internally.
2) Canary deploy runtime-1.19 with feature flag on 1% of traffic (internal + low-risk customer endpoints) for 48h; monitor short-request p99 and fairness index.
3) If stable, increase to 10% for 24h and run targeted loadgen compare runs.
4) Gradual global rollout to Hosted and Dedicated over 7 days with automated rollback if alarms triggered.
5) For Private customers, provide a patch bundle and opt-in instructions; schedule assisted rollout for customers who reported incidents.
qa_plan: Run the mixed-length scenario from loadgen (see steps_to_repro) in the CI integration environment and in canary cluster. Validate metrics pre/post: short-request latency histogram, batch composition distribution, KV-cache hit rate, and per-tenant in-flight token counters. Run a chaos experiment that forces KV eviction to validate reserve prevents starvation.
notes: - Trade-offs: short-request reserve reduces available capacity for throughput-oriented long batches; mitigations include making reserve small and configurable per-tenant tier.
- This change touches admission logic and KV-cache heuristics; coordinate with SRE for memory tuning during rollout.
- Consider a follow-up to expose per-route QoS config in the Console for customers to opt into latency-first behavior.
- Related customer threads: #eng-esc-hosted-longtail (Slack), case RED-3492 (Dedicated customer).
comments: 2025-02-11 Ayesha Khan: Triage - customer RED-3492 reported sudden p99 regressions on hosted model m-gpt-large. Initial traces attached. Marking P0 due to customer impact and multiple affected tenants.

2025-02-12 Liam Carter: Investigation - reproduced locally using mixed-length loadgen. Observed KV eviction spikes correlated with long-batch runtime. Created reproducible harness and captured flamegraphs. See attachment.

2025-02-13 Mei Chen (SRE): Observability - added temporary Grafana panels for per-tenant in-flight tokens and a fairness index. Alert rule 'scheduler.short_request_starvation' created at warning threshold.

2025-02-14 Liam Carter: Design note - proposing per-tenant short-request reserve + admission score decay. Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INFER-366. Requesting review from Runtime and SRE.

2025-02-15 Fernando Ruiz (Runtime): Review - Concern about increasing GC pressure if reserve leads to more small batches; recommend also capping microbatch rate and adding backpressure when reserve depleted.

2025-02-16 Liam Carter: Implementation - pushed WIP branch and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1428. Added unit tests for scoring function and deterministic scheduler sim.

2025-02-18 QA (Nina Patel): QA pass - integration harness shows p99 improved from 720ms to 140ms under attacker mix in local env. Noted a small (1.8%) throughput drop on long batches at 90th percentile.
2025-02-19 PM (Olivia Martins): Stakeholder update - informed affected customers of patch ETA and scheduled private deployment assistance slots. Preparing release notes.
2025-02-20 Release Lead (Carlos Gomez): Pre-canary checklist complete. Feature flag toggles added to console flags UI. Proceeding to 1% canary today 18:00 UTC.
